name: A valet, Cannes
bio: A young manservant Wilde saw at the Bataille des Fleurs at Cannes on 1 February 1899, riding on the box of his employer's carriage beside the coachman, wreathed in flowers. Wilde described him to Robert Ross the next day as 'a very handsome boy' and answered the tableau with a phrase — 'Imperial, Neronian Rome'. Nothing else about him survives: not his name, not his age, and no suggestion the two ever spoke.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Robert Ross, 2 February 1899, Napoule, Complete Letters printed 1121 (PDF 1167, folio confirmed on the rendered page image). A CITATION CORRECTION: the 2026-08-04 sweep placed this passage at 'printed ~p. 1119'. It is printed 1121; the OCR mirror's page attribution drifts by a page or two here and the folio was confirmed from the page itself.
